items.t: 30/500: severe pain. Codeine component: acute moderate pain not relieved by paracetamol or ibuprofen alone, in patients over 12 years.

src.q: For the relief of severe pain.

items.t: Adults: 2 tablets not more often than every 4-6 hours; maximum 8 tablets in 24 hours. Elderly: as adults, but a reduced dose may be needed.

items.t: Keep treatment as short as possible; agree a treatment plan and end-of-treatment plan before starting; taper gradually when stopping.

src.q: The duration of treatment should be as short as possible

items.t: Under 12 years: should not be used (risk of opioid toxicity from variable codeine-to-morphine metabolism).

src.q: Codeine should not be used in children below the age of 12 years because of the risk of opioid toxicity due to the variable and unpredictable metabolism of codeine to morphine

items.t: 12-15 years: 1 tablet every 6 hours when necessary, maximum 4 tablets in 24 hours. 16-18 years: 1-2 tablets every 6 hours when necessary, maximum 8 tablets in 24 hours. 30/500: no more than 3 days without consulting a doctor.

src.q: Children aged 12 to 15 years: One tablet every 6 hours when necessary to a maximum of 4 tablets in 24 hours.
Children aged 16 to 18 years : One to two tablets every 6 hours when necessary up to a maximum of 8 tablets in 24 hours.
Do not take for more than 3 days without consulting your doctor.

items.t: Sleep-related breathing disorders (central sleep apnoea): consider reducing the opioid dose.
